content: (i) Idea of a set defined by a property, Set notations and their meanings.
(ii) Disjoint sets, Universal set and complement of set
(iii) Venn diagrams, Use of sets and Venn diagrams to solve problems.
(iv) Commutative and Associative laws, Distributive properties over union and intersection.
topics.notes: Set notations e.g. (x : x is real), ∪, ∩, {}, ∉, ∈, ⊂, ⊆, U (universal set), A’ (complement). More challenging problems involving union, intersection, universal set, subset, complement. Three set problems. Use of De Morgan’s laws.

content: Surds of the form √a and a + b√c where a is rational, b is a positive integer and n is not a perfect square.
topics.notes: All four operations on surds. Rationalising the denominator of surds such as √a/√b, etc.

content: Properties: Closure, Commutativity, Associativity and Distributivity, Identity elements and inverses.
topics.notes: Use of properties to solve related problems.

content: (i) Rule of syntax: true or false statements, rule of logic applied to arguments, implications and deductions.
topics.notes: Using logical reasoning to determine validity of compound statements. Symbols: ~P, ∨, ∧, ⇒. Use of truth tables including negation.

content: (i) Domain and co-domain of a function.
(ii) One-to-one, onto, identity and constant mapping.
topics.notes: Notation e.g. f: x → 3x+4. Graphical representation, image and range. Determination of inverse of one-to-one functions. Notation fog(x) = f(g(x)). Restrict to simple algebraic functions.

Recognition and sketching of graphs. Gradient, intercepts, parallel/perpendicular lines, linear inequalities and Linear Programming. Vertex, axis of symmetry, max/min for quadratics. Completing the square, roots (discriminant), sum/product of roots. Cubic graphs, factorization, remainder/factor theorems.

content: (i) Rational functions of the form Q(x) = g(x)/f(x) where g(x) and f(x) are polynomials.
(ii) Resolution of rational functions into partial fractions.
topics.notes: Factorisation into linear/quadratic factors (degree numerator < denominator ≤4). Basic operations, zeros, domain, range (sketching not required).
Laws of indices, solving equations. Laws of logarithms, calculations, change of base, solving equations. Reduction of relations like y = ax^b to linear form. Graphs of logarithmic functions.

content: (ii) Simple cases of selection of objects.
topics.notes: Notations nPr and nCr. Examples with/without replacement.
For positive integral index only. Use of (1+x)^n ≈ 1 + nx for small x. Proof required.

content: (ii) Linear sequence/Arithmetic Progression (A.P.) and Geometric Progression (G.P.).
(iv) Linear series (sum of A.P.) and exponential series (sum of G.P.).
topics.notes: General terms, sums. Sum to infinity for |r|<1. Generating terms and explicit formulas for recurrence.
Order, equality, operations up to 3x3. Determinants 2x2 and 3x3. Solution of simultaneous equations. Images under transformation, inverse, composition. Specific reflections and rotations.
General angles, specific values (30°,45°,60°), identities, negative angles, radians. Compound angle formulae. Graphs, solving equations. Relation to coordinates on circle.

Midpoint, distance, gradient, equations, parallel/perpendicular, angle between lines, distance from point to line. Circle equations, tangents/normals. Parabola equations, parametric, tangents/normals.

content: (vii) Second order derivatives and Rates of change, Maxima and Minima
topics.notes: From first principles (simple). Rules including chain. Implicit e.g. ax² + by² = c. Transcendental (exp, ln). Tangents, turning points, curve sketching, kinematics.
Polynomials (power rule), substitution, trig. Areas, volumes of revolution, kinematics, trapezium rule.

content: (i) Tabulation and Graphical representation of data
topics.notes: Frequency/cumulative tables, histograms, ogives. Mean, median, mode, quartiles. Range, IQR, mean deviation, variance, SD. Scatter diagrams, line of best fit, Spearman’s rank.

content: (iii) Calculation of Probability using simple sample spaces.
topics.notes: Equally likely, mutually exclusive, independent, conditional. Binomial and Poisson distributions (simple cases).

content: (i) Definitions of scalar and vector quantities.
topics.notes: ai + bj form, laws, unit vectors, position/midpoint, composition (forces), dot product (angle, trig formulae).

content: (iii) Composition and resolution of coplanar forces.
topics.notes: Resultants, Lami’s theorem, principles of moments, coefficient of friction.
Displacement, velocity, acceleration, Newton’s laws, inclined planes, gravity. v=u+at, etc. Conservation of momentum. Projectiles at angle to horizontal.

notes: Topics marked with * are for Section B of Paper 2 only. More challenging questions may be set on General Mathematics topics. Asterisks *** or **** indicate country-specific topics.
